skill.name: evidence-verification
skill.description: Guides AI agents to verify completed work by collecting test, build, lint, deployment, and quality evidence before closing tasks.
skill.summary: Evidence-first checklist and templates for proving development work is complete.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

content.value_statement: AI agents can mark tasks complete without proof. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to collect test, build, and quality evidence.
actual_capabilities: Provides evidence templates for tests, builds, code quality checks, and task completion.
Defines minimum, production-grade, and gold quality standards.
Lists verification workflows for implementation, code review, and deployment.
Supplies checklists for capturing exit codes, timestamps, coverage, and artifacts.
Includes example evidence reports for successful and failed test or build runs.
limitations: It does not run verification commands automatically.
It cannot prove evidence authenticity beyond recorded command output.
Teams must adapt templates to their project tools and quality gates.
Deployment guidance still requires normal permissions and change controls.

use_cases.title: Finish implementation with proof
use_cases.description: Collect test, build, lint, and type-check evidence before marking a feature complete.

use_cases.title: Review agent work
use_cases.description: Check whether another agent supplied enough evidence to support its completion claims.

use_cases.title: Prepare release verification
use_cases.description: Document pre-deployment checks, health checks, smoke tests, and rollback readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Collect basic evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner verification after a small code change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the evidence-verification skill to list the minimum checks for this task and record the results I provide.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a completed task
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this completed task using the skill. Identify missing test, build, lint, or timestamp evidence before approval.

prompt_templates.title: Build a quality evidence report
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured evidence collection for a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise evidence report for this change. Include commands run, exit codes, coverage, artifacts, warnings, and conclusion.

prompt_templates.title: Audit release readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply production-grade verification standards to this release. Separate passed checks, failed checks, missing evidence, and required follow-up.

output_examples.input: The user asks whether a login feature is ready for review.
output_examples.output: A short evidence summary lists passing tests, successful build, lint status, coverage, timestamp, and a ready-for-review conclusion.

output_examples.input: The user provides a failed build transcript.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the failed checks, cites the exit code, summarizes the build errors, and states that the task is not complete.

output_examples.input: The user requests deployment verification guidance.
output_examples.output: The response organizes pre-deployment checks, deployment result evidence, health checks, smoke tests, and rollback verification.

best_practices: Record command names, exit codes, timestamps, and key output for every verification run.
Treat failed or missing evidence as a blocker until it is fixed or explicitly accepted.
Match the evidence standard to the risk of the task, from minimum to production-grade.
anti_patterns: Do not claim tests passed without recording command output and exit codes.
Do not reuse old evidence after changing relevant code.
Do not mark production work complete when build, security, or deployment checks failed.

faq.question: Does this skill execute tests or builds?
faq.answer: No. It gives templates and workflows for documenting verification results from commands that the user or agent runs.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It is tool-agnostic and includes examples for JavaScript, Python, Rust, Go, and deployment workflows.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is written for AI agents and can guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code sessions.

faq.question: What evidence is required at minimum?
faq.answer: At minimum, one verification check should run, with its exit code, timestamp, and result recorded.

faq.question: How should failed evidence be handled?
faq.answer: Failed evidence should block completion until the issue is fixed or the user explicitly accepts the risk.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for CI?
faq.answer: No. It complements CI by helping agents report clear evidence from local, CI, or deployment checks.
